conviction_note: The company's own documents lean modestly positive: H1 organic growth near 20%, pricing actions, a FY guide the CEO called conservative while the CFO argued for a raise, and $190M of annualized acquired revenue signed with 16 of 19 deals closed by 2 Nov, against an August inorganic assumption of $25-30M. That argues for a beat and a raise. Against it: the stock is +48% since the $44 secondary, +13% over 20 days, 1% off its high and above the average sell-side target, and the last two prints were sold (-3.4% after a 7% revenue beat with a reaffirmed guide). So p_up is only 56 on an abs move of 6 (no option chain; median reaction 3.4, raised because a guide change is likely and about 15% of float is short). impact_sum +1.4 and the scaled +0.72 agree in sign; the scaled number is smaller because the beats-sold history goes into p_up.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus $340.31M, adjusted EPS $1.12-1.13. FXEmpire (https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/andg/earnings) and MarketBeat/Chartmill (per search snippets) agree; one other source has $333.6M and EPS $0.90 on 2 estimates. Chartmill notes the revenue estimate was revised down 1.13% over 3 months. No company Q3 guide was given on the 2026-08-12 call. FY2026 company guide is revenue ~$980M-$1B and adj. EBITDA $225-250M, reaffirmed 2026-08-12 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002065708/000119312526346839/d122909dex991.htm). Prior year Q3 2025 revenue $284.29M (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/andg/financials/?p=quarterly), so the bar is +19.7% y/y. H1 2026 was $458.4M (+19.4%), so the FY guide implies H2 growth of only +14.7% to +19.1%.
positioning_check: No listed option chain (baseline options status no_options_market), so there is no skew to read. FINRA short interest per equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/andg/shortinterest): 2,619,901 shares at 2026-10-30 settlement, 7.71 days to cover, up from 1,945,580 on 2026-09-15. Public Class A float is roughly 17.6M (12.65M IPO shares, https://investor.andersen.com/news-events/investor-press-releases/detail/245/andersen-announces-closing-of-its-initial-public-offering-and-full-exercise-of-the-underwriters-over-allotment-option, plus the 4.93M-share Aug secondary), so short interest is about 15% of float (my estimate; MarketBeat's 2.81% uses total shares). Tape: spot $66.72, run-up +13.2% over 20 days, 1.1% below the 52-week high, +264% off the low. Sell-side average target $61.29 (high $78) per investing.com, below spot.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue is likely to clear the $340.3M bar (+19.7% y/y) by about 2-3%. In Q2 organic growth was 20.6% and total growth 23.7% (Q2 printed $217.7M against a $190-205M company guide and ~$203M consensus). H1 billing rate per hour was up 10.1%, a further rate adjustment took effect in July, and a 3% technology surcharge applies to contracts signed from Q2. The CEO called July 'strong' and Q3 the seasonally largest quarter. Deals closed in Q2 and Q3 (Ireland, NZ, Nigeria, Uruguay, Switzerland, Canada) add a few points of inorganic growth. My estimate is ~$345-352M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue beat consensus by ~7% and the company guide's top end by $13M, FY guide reaffirmed, stock -3.4% (2026-08-12 to 08-13, baseline). Q1 2026: -2.42%. Q4 2025 (first print): +13.58%. Revenue beats have been sold since the first print.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at +19.7% sits roughly at the Q2 organic rate and gives little credit for the July rate step-up, the surcharge or Q3-closed acquisitions. Chartmill shows the estimate revised DOWN 1.13% over 3 months. If the market had priced a ~$350M quarter, the published estimates would have drifted up rather than down. The +13% 20-day run-up says the buy side may already be above the published bar.
findings.independence: Q2 release (company 8-K exhibit, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002065708/000119312526346839/d122909dex991.htm) for the $217.7M and the closed-deal list. Investing.com for the Q2 guide of $190-205M (https://www.investing.com/equities/andersen-group-corp). The transcript and the release are both company sources from the same day.

findings.finding: A FY2026 guidance raise is likely, on two lines. (1) EBITDA: on the 2026-08-12 call the CFO advocated raising the $225-250M adj. EBITDA guide and the CEO declined as 'conservative'. William Blair pointed out that the guide implies a y/y step-down in H2, even though H1 adj. EBITDA margin was 26.8% and Q3 is the peak quarter. (2) Revenue: in August inorganic 2026 revenue was cut to $25-30M (from $55M) on closing delays. Since then, signed deals grew from 16 (~$134M annualized at 5 Oct) to 19 (~$190M at 15 Oct), with 13 closed by 15 Oct and 16 of 19 closed by 2 Nov. About $150M+ annualized closing in October implies roughly $30M of Q4 inorganic revenue alone, above the $25-30M full-year assumption.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No raise yet in this name's short public history. Q2 2026 reaffirmed (not raised) despite a beat and fell -3.4%; Simply Wall St (https://www.webull.ca/news-detail/15398616540914688, 2026-08-14) attributed the pullback to management 'holding full year guidance' rather than raising.
findings.why_not_priced: Published FY revenue consensus still sits at the $980M-$1B guide (Benzinga lists $980M-1B), and the Q3 estimate was revised down. If the closings had been carried into models, FY estimates would sit above the guide. The run-up from $53 (25 Sep) to $66.7 suggests some of the buy side expects the raise. The pull on this finding is that a raise of only ~$15-25M (1.5-2.5%) may be what holders already want, which is why it is not sized larger.
findings.independence: Separate company documents: the 2026-08-12 call transcript (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262105210-tradingkey) for the EBITDA-raise debate and the $25-30M inorganic assumption, and the 5 Oct / 2 Nov releases (https://investor.andersen.com/news-events/investor-press-releases/detail/260/andersen-completes-uk-acquisition-expanding-presence-in-key-global-market, https://investor.andersen.com/news-events/investor-press-releases/detail/266/andersen-group-closes-three-strategic-acquisitions-further-accelerating-global-expansion) for signed and closed counts. All are company sources, and the inorganic arithmetic is my inference.

findings.finding: On 10 Nov, two days before the print, the company signed five more deals (~$38.1M annualized, U.S., India, Europe) expected to close Q1 2027. That takes 2026 signings to 24 transactions and ~$228M annualized, against the 'at least $100M annualized excluded from 2026' cited in August. This is a visible 2027 inorganic tailwind management is likely to frame on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No 2027 outlook has been given yet. The stock reaction to deal announcements is not isolated in the sources.
findings.why_not_priced: The release is two days old and gives no 2027 number. Sell-side targets (avg $61.29) predate it. It matters only if management quantifies a 2027 framework on the call.
findings.independence: Same company release series as finding 2 but a different fact (2027 closings rather than 2026). It is not counted in the 2026 inorganic arithmetic above.

findings.finding: Short interest rose into the print: 2.62M shares at 30 Oct settlement (7.71 days to cover), up from 1.95M on 15 Sep. That is about 15% of the ~17.6M-share public Class A float. A beat-and-raise has squeeze fuel behind it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. The stock rose from $53 to $66.7 since late September while short interest climbed, so shorts are already under water.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is not in the sealed baseline, and the commonly quoted short % (2.81% at MarketBeat) divides by all ~113M shares including Class B, which understates crowding in the tradable float. Short interest at 7.7 days to cover would not have built further into the high if the shorts thought the setup was clean.
findings.independence: IPO closing release for the float numerator (https://investor.andersen.com/news-events/investor-press-releases/detail/245/andersen-announces-closing-of-its-initial-public-offering-and-full-exercise-of-the-underwriters-over-allotment-option) and secondary closing (https://investor.andersen.com/news-events/investor-press-releases/detail/259/andersen-announces-closing-of-secondary-offering-and-full-exercise-of-the-underwriters-option-to-purchase-additional-shares). The float estimate is mine.

findings.finding: The stock goes into the print at $66.72, 1.1% off its 52-week high, +13.2% over 20 days, about +48% above the $44 August secondary (sold by management and directors) and above the average sell-side target of $61.29 (5 Buy / 3 Hold; high $78 Truist-era). Much of a beat-and-raise looks bought, and this name sold its last two beats.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: 7% beat, -3.4%. Q1 2026: -2.42%. The 2026-08-14 Simply Wall St piece notes the stock had risen 37.6% in three months before the Q2 print and was sold.
findings.why_not_priced: This IS the price. The finding says the bar the stock must clear is higher than the published consensus, so a modest beat-and-raise can be sold. With price targets below spot, a raise has to come with target increases to sustain the level.
findings.independence: Baseline tape (run-up, 52w high) and Truist raise to $70 on 2026-09-25 at $53.08 (search snippet, MarketBeat). Same theme as the reaction-history veto, counted once here.

findings.finding: Margin and GAAP noise risk: 16 acquisitions closed largely in October (consulting-heavy, U.S. Andersen Consulting firms plus UK, Netherlands, Italy, South Africa), and the August guide already implies an H2 EBITDA step-down. Integration costs, lower-margin consulting mix and equity comp (the reason Q2 was a GAAP loss) could dilute the Q4 margin commentary even if revenue is raised.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's GAAP loss (equity comp) sat beside a 54% adj. EBITDA increase and the stock fell -3.4%. It is unclear which line drove that.
findings.why_not_priced: Inference only. No company number quantifies integration cost or acquired-margin dilution. If the market had priced it, the EBITDA estimates would not imply the margin expansion the CFO argued for.
findings.independence: The William Blair question on the H2 EBITDA step-down in the 2026-08-12 transcript (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262105210-tradingkey). This partly offsets finding 2's EBITDA leg and is kept small for that reason.

findings.finding: On 6 Oct the company disclosed the close of a forensic investigation into a social-engineering incident: one employee targeted, files of a small number of clients accessed, no operational impact, and no material financial impact expected. A ransomware-claims site lists Andersen (SilentRansomGroup, 8 Oct), unverified.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and called immaterial by the company. It matters only if the 10-Q adds a contingency or a client-loss disclosure.

findings.finding: Peer read: CBIZ, the largest listed U.S. accounting/tax peer, reported Q3 2026 revenue of $702.2M, +1.2% y/y, below estimates. That is weak industry-level demand for tax and accounting services this season. CBIZ is mid-merger (Grant Thornton deal) and structurally slow-growing, so the read to a 20% organic grower is weak.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history of ANDG reacting to CBIZ prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer print that landed after ANDG last spoke, but ANDG traded up through it, so the market has visibly looked through it.
findings.independence: Proxy only. Quiver (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/CBIZ+Q3+Revenue+Reaches+%24702+Million+as+Net+Income+Rises+57%25) carries the same numbers.

baseline_tension: No skew to read. The positive fundamental lean (beat plus a likely raise) agrees with the +13% 20-day run-up and the near-high price, which is exactly the setup in which this name sold its last two beats. That pulls p_up toward 50, partly offset by about 15% of float short with short interest rising.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; beats sold): reported-quarter beat finding cut from +1.0 to +0.6; p_up 57 -> 56
Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives; ~15% of float short, 7.7 days to cover): run-up/valuation negative -1.0 -> -0.8 and integration/margin negative -0.5 -> -0.4
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): bar sourced to two agreeing estimate sources ($340.31M), so no cap; all findings resolve inside the window
Lesson 5 (proxy): CBIZ peer read kept small at -0.2 with independence labelled proxy; guidance finding left at +1.5 because it rests on company documents
